description:
Create a Stripe embedded-checkout link, only when the customer asks to pay.

The payment link is the order: the customer sees it here for the first time.
It attaches each cart line's design and checks its print file. The link locks
each line to its design for good, so never create it just because the customer
picked or finished a design.

Every line needs artwork first: a design, or the customer's own finished file
uploaded through `order_get_artwork_upload_page`. `LinesWithoutArtworkError`
names the lines that have none. A line whose design was made before the
product was chosen needs `design_adapt` first (`AdaptStepRequiredError`). Each design goes on with its latest version.
`CheckoutRenderFailedError` names a line whose print file failed: that line
needs new artwork. Any other failure keeps what was done, so call again once
the cause is fixed. `NoSnapshotError`
means a design is not saved yet; a photo book can take a few minutes after it
resolves. Wait a little and call this again.

A product added to the cart after another line was designed or got its upload
page needs a checkout link of its own: `other_lines` names those products. Tell
the customer they need a new checkout link, and call this again when they ask
to pay for them. Pass `order_id` only to pay an order that already had a
payment link.

Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED for the `checkout_url`. Put
`checkout_url` in your reply as a markdown hyperlink (never the raw URL),
and call `order_get` yourself to confirm payment. When the payment card is
displayed, it shows a "Pay securely" button wired to the link and polls
`order_get` itself once clicked, so just confirm the payment step is ready
and share the link again only if the customer asks for it. From here on, `reference_id` is
the customer's order reference.
name: order_create_payment_link

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Create a payment link
